title: Minimum Partition Difference
statement:
A cargo plane carries `n` pieces of luggage. The `i`-th piece weighs `weights[i]`. The cargo hold has two compartments, a left one and a right one, and **every** piece of luggage must be placed in exactly one of them.

Distribute the luggage so that the difference between the total weight in the left compartment and the total weight in the right compartment is as small as possible. Print that smallest difference (it is never negative, so the difference is taken as an absolute value). Either compartment may end up empty.

The input contains several independent test cases; answer each one.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `T`, the number of test cases.
For each test case, the first line contains `n` and the second line contains `n` space-separated integers `weights[0], ..., weights[n-1]`.
outputFormat: For each test case print one line with the minimum possible difference.

examples.explanation: Four test cases. (1) {3, 3, 3} = 9 against {7, 1} = 8, difference 1. (2) {10, 11} = 21 against {7, 7, 7} = 21, difference 0. (3) {1, 1, 1, 1, 1} = 5 against {8} = 8, difference 3. (4) {2, 4, 2} = 8 against {3, 5} = 8, difference 0.
A single piece can only go to one side, leaving a difference of 5. With three equal pieces the best split is 8 against 4, a difference of 4.

complexity.time: O(n · S) per test case, S = sum of weights

hints: If one compartment weighs L and the total is S, the difference is |S - 2L|. So you want L as close to S / 2 as possible.
This is a subset-sum question: which totals L can be formed by some subset of the weights? A boolean table over sums (or one big bitmask) answers it.
Build the set of reachable sums one weight at a time, then scan down from floor(S / 2) to find the largest reachable L; the answer is S - 2L.
